title: Lumbar puncture
what: A thin needle in the lower back takes a little of the fluid around the spinal cord and brain. The needle goes in below the end of the spinal cord, so the cord itself is not touched.
why: When infection or inflammation of the brain lining is suspected, for some nervous system diseases, and sometimes to give medicine.
duration: the puncture usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, then about an hour of rest
tell_doctor: Blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Allergy to numbing medicines or antiseptics
If you have back pain or have had spine surgery

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Sometimes a blood test and a head scan are done first. The doctor decides.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat and drink as normal. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Consent
prepare.text: The doctor will explain why you need the puncture and ask you to sign a consent form. Ask all your questions.

bring: Someone to go with you, if you go home the same day
steps: You lie on your side and pull your knees to your chest, or sit and bend your back forward
The skin on your lower back is cleaned with antiseptic
The doctor puts a thin needle between the bones of the spine
A few drops of fluid drip into test tubes
The needle is removed and the spot is covered with a plaster
feel: Then a feeling of pressure in your back
Sometimes a quick shooting feeling goes down your leg. Tell the doctor
It is important to lie still
after: You are usually asked to lie down for about an hour
You may get a headache that is worse when standing. It usually passes in a few days
No heavy activity for 1 to 2 days
The test result takes from a few hours to a few days
red_flags: A fever, strong back pain, or a headache that does not ease when lying down
Numbness or weakness in the legs, or problems passing urine
Fluid or blood leaking from the puncture spot

faq.a: Serious problems are rare. The most common one is a headache for a few days.

faq.q: Why does my head hurt after the puncture?
faq.a: A little fluid may leak through the puncture. Rest and drinking help. If the pain is strong, tell your doctor.
